properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 13 at 8:40PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Sanford
to reach Minor Flood Stage. The river is forecast to remain steady
around Minor Flood Stage into next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Sanford...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.5 feet, Water surrounds homes and covers some
driveways in the Stone Island area near Enterprise in Volusia
County. Water enters yards and floods docks in the River Oaks
Estates subdivision.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Friday the stage was 5.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to remain steady near 5.5 feet
through the weekend and into next week.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday afternoon at noon EST.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 13 at 8:35PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Geneva
Above Lake Harney to reach Moderate Flood Stage. River levels are
expected to remain steady into next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Moderate
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Water enters the first story of homes on
Whitcomb Drive between Crossover Lane and Lake Harney Road. Water
covers Mullet Lake Park.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Friday the stage was 9.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Friday was 9.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain nearly steady around
9.1 through the weekend and into next week.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday afternoon at 1215 PM EST.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 13 at 8:29PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Recent extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River
has caused the river near Cocoa to rise to Major Flood Stage around
17.1 feet. Additional small rises are possible through the weekend
into next week, before river levels could begin to decline by late
next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM EST Friday the stage was 17.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 PM EST Friday was 17.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to rise to a crest of 17.2 feet
this weekend, hold steady around this level into next week, then
could begin to decline by late next week.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday afternoon at noon EST.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 13 at 8:21PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.On the St Johns River at Astor, slight rises within Minor Flood
Stage are forecast this weekend into next week due to a combination
of northerly winds, downstream tidal effects, and water from upstream
heavy rainfall working north through the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.possible

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Friday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Friday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to rise slightly while remaining
in Minor Flood Stage through this weekend and into next week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday afternoon at noon EST.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued November 13 at 4:56PM PST until November 13 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Portions of Placer, Sacramento, Amador, El Dorado and
Nevada County in California...

* WHEN...Until 700 PM PST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 454 PM PST, local law enforcement continues to report
flooding in the advisory area, and additional bands of
rainfall continue to move into the area. This is causing
urban and small stream flooding. Between 0.5 and 1.5 inches
of rain have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Auburn, Placerville, Jackson, Cameron Park, El Dorado Hills,
Lake Of The Pines, Ione, Rancho Murieta, Colfax, Shingle
Springs, Rescue, Coloma, Lotus, Latrobe, Smithflat, Garden
Valley, Pilot Hill, Greenwood and Forest Home.
- Highway 50 and Interstate 80
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.
properties.area: Amador, CA; El Dorado, CA; Nevada, CA; Placer, CA; Sacramento, CA

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued November 13 at 5:31PM CST until November 14 at 9:00AM CST by NWS Chicago IL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Extreme Southeast Central Cook County in northeastern
Illinois...
Central Lake IN County in northwestern Indiana...

* WHEN...Until 900 AM CST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding
may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains and
ditches may be clogged with leaf debris increasing the risk of
flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 530 PM CST, Doppler radar indicated lake effect rain. Minor
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory
area. Several creeks and streams are rising, including the Turkey
Creek near Merrillville which has recently risen above bankfull.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Chicago, Hammond, Gary, Calumet City, Merrillville, South Shore,
East Chicago, Schererville, Hobart, Lansing, Crown Point,
Highland, Munster, Cedar Lake, Griffith, Dyer, South Deering, St.
John, Lake Station, Lynwood, Lakes of the Four Seasons, Whiting,
Winfield and New Chicago.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
A Flood Advisory means minor flooding along waterways and other poor
drainage areas is imminent or may already be occurring. Persons in
the advisory area should use caution and avoid flood waters.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 13 at 8:17AM CST until November 18 at 2:00PM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Tilden...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...From Sunday afternoon to Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to
below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill.
Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well
away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM CST Friday the stage was 10.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
Sunday afternoon to a crest of 15.0 feet Monday morning. It will
then fall below flood stage late Tuesday evening.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 15.2
feet on 09/19/1983.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 12 at 11:41AM MST until November 17 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1140 AM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue
with flow peaking at 3000 cfs.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
